# GitHub Actions (test matrix and NuGet Trusted Publishing release) (tooling)

<!-- Generated by `stackfoundry pack render` from a researched pack. Each rule cites [key] = a source below.
     Disagree with a rule? Record the repo's way in the pack's repoConvention and re-render, so a refresh keeps
     your decision. -->

Applies to: client. Versions in use: actions/checkout@v6.0.2 (.github/workflows/tests.yml, .github/workflows/deploy.yml); actions/setup-dotnet@v5.2.0 (.github/workflows/tests.yml, .github/workflows/deploy.yml); actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.1 (.github/workflows/deploy.yml (build-package)); actions/download-artifact@v8.0.1 (.github/workflows/deploy.yml (publish)); cardinalby/git-tag-action@v1.0 (.github/workflows/deploy.yml (tag)); NuGet/login@v1 (.github/workflows/deploy.yml (publish)).

## Rules

- **Pass secrets, inputs and step outputs to scripts only through `env:`, and read them as variables (`$env:NAME` in pwsh, `"$NAME"` in bash). Never write `${{ secrets.* }}`, `${{ inputs.* }}`, `${{ github.event.* }}` or `${{ steps.*.outputs.* }}` inside a `run:` body.** Expressions are substituted into the script text before the shell starts. A `notifyUrl` input containing `"` or `$(...)` runs arbitrary PowerShell in a job that holds AUTH_KEY/AUTH_SECRET. A secret containing `$` or a backtick is expanded inside the pwsh double-quoted string, so the tests silently get wrong credentials. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: jobs.test-linux / jobs.test-netfx step 'Create Test Settings' (secrets.AUTH_KEY, secrets.AUTH_SECRET, inputs.notifyUrl inline); .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.tag step 'Check Existing Tag' (steps.get_version.outputs.version inline); .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.publish step 'Publish NuGet packages to NuGet' (steps.login.outputs.NUGET_API_KEY inline). [gh-script-injection, gh-secure-use, gh-use-secrets]
  This repo: Known deviation: tests.yml 'Create Test Settings' interpolates secrets and inputs.notifyUrl into the pwsh script, deploy.yml 'Check Existing Tag' interpolates a step output, and the publish step passes the NuGet key inline (as in NuGet's own example). Fix: move each value to the step's `env:` block and reference `$env:AUTH_KEY`, `$env:AUTH_SECRET`, `$env:NOTIFY_URL`, `"$VERSION"` and `"$NUGET_API_KEY"`.
- **Keep the workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` default and raise scopes per job, only on the job that needs them. Every new job either inherits read-only or declares a complete block.** As soon as a job sets any scope, every scope it does not list becomes `none`, so a partial block can break a step. Raising scopes at workflow level gives write or OIDC access to every job, including the six live-API test legs. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: permissions; .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: permissions, jobs.tag.permissions (contents: write), jobs.publish.permissions (id-token: write). [gh-secure-use, gh-workflow-syntax]
- **Remove `actions: write` from build-package and `actions: read` from publish unless a step is shown to need them. Artifacts uploaded and downloaded in the same run need no token scope.** `actions: write` lets any step in the job act on workflow runs (the docs give cancelling a run as the example). download-artifact needs a token with `actions: read` only for artifacts from another run or repository. The extra scopes widen what a compromised action in the release jobs can do. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.build-package.permissions.actions, jobs.publish.permissions.actions. [gh-workflow-syntax, download-readme, upload-readme]
- **Grant `id-token: write` only on the job that runs NuGet/login, never at workflow level and never on test or build jobs. Keep NuGet/login and `dotnet nuget push` together in that one job.** nuget.org issues a push key to any OIDC token whose claims match the policy (repo owner, repo, workflow file, optional environment). Any step in a job with `id-token: write` and `environment: Release` inside deploy.yml can mint such a token. The key lasts 1 hour and each token yields exactly one key, so requesting it in an earlier job or passing it through outputs or artifacts either leaks it or lets it expire. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.publish (permissions.id-token, step 'NuGet login (OIDC)', step 'Publish NuGet packages to NuGet'). [nuget-tp, nuget-login, gh-workflow-syntax]
- **Treat the file name `deploy.yml`, the environment name `Release` on the publish job and the repository owner/name as part of the nuget.org Trusted Publishing policy. Update the policy on nuget.org before renaming any of them, and before moving the publish job into a reusable workflow.** The policy matches the workflow file name only (no path, case-insensitive) and, when set, the environment. A mismatch makes NuGet/login fail with no matching policy, and the release is blocked. How nuget.org matches a job inside a called reusable workflow is not documented, so treat that move as breaking until it is verified. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.publish (environment: Release). [nuget-tp]
- **Restrict which branches can publish through the `Release` environment's deployment-branches rule, not in the workflow. The Trusted Publishing policy has no branch field, and deploy.yml can be dispatched from any ref.** Without a branch rule, anyone with write access can run NuGet Deploy from a feature branch and publish its build to nuget.org under the trusted policy. Required reviewers also hold back environment secrets until approval, and the user who started the run cannot approve it. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: on.workflow_dispatch, jobs.publish.environment (repository environment settings are not visible in the repo). [nuget-tp, gh-environments]
- **Pin every action, first-party (actions/*) included, to a full-length commit SHA with a trailing version comment (`uses: actions/checkout@<40-char sha> # v6.0.2`), or onboard both workflows to the workflow lockfile (.github/workflows/actions.lock, GA since 2026-10-28). Keep the pins current with Dependabot version updates for the `github-actions` ecosystem.** Tags can be moved or deleted by whoever controls the action repo, so a tag pin lets code change in the release job without a commit here. NuGet/login runs in the job that holds `id-token: write` and receives the push key. git-tag-action runs with `contents: write`. Dependabot does not raise alerts for SHA-pinned actions, so pins without version updates go stale silently. The lockfile also pins transitive actions and satisfies the 'require full-length SHA' policy, but it does not pin `jobs.<id>.uses` reusable-workflow calls (the local `./.github/workflows/tests.yml` call is unaffected). Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: every `uses:` (actions/checkout@v6.0.2, actions/setup-dotnet@v5.2.0); .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: every `uses:` (actions/checkout, setup-dotnet, upload-artifact, download-artifact, cardinalby/git-tag-action@v1.0, NuGet/login@v1); no .github/dependabot.yml exists. [gh-secure-use, gh-lockfiles, gh-lockfiles-ga, gh-sha-policy]
  This repo: Known deviation: first-party actions are pinned to semver tags (actions/checkout@v6.0.2, actions/setup-dotnet@v5.2.0, actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.1, actions/download-artifact@v8.0.1), and the third-party actions to moving tags (NuGet/login@v1, cardinalby/git-tag-action@v1.0) in .github/workflows/tests.yml and deploy.yml. There is no .github/dependabot.yml. Fix: replace each `@<tag>` with the full commit SHA that tag resolves to in the action's own repository, plus a `# <tag>` comment (or generate .github/workflows/actions.lock with `gh actions-lock`). Then add .github/dependabot.yml with a `github-actions` update entry and, optionally, enable the repository's 'require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA' policy.
- **Do not depend on cardinalby/git-tag-action for release correctness. Prefer a `run:` step that does `git tag` and `git push origin <tag>` using checkout's persisted credentials (the tag job already has `contents: write` and `fetch-depth: 0`), or verify afterwards that the tag exists and points at the built commit.** The action's entrypoint has no `set -e` and calls the refs API with `curl -s` without `-f`, never checking the response, so a failed tag creation still passes the step. When the tag already exists locally it PATCHes it with `force: true`, which moves an existing release tag; only the repo's guard step prevents that. It is a Docker action rebuilt on every run from an unpinned `alpine` base with `apk add` at run time, from a low-adoption fork of an action its own README calls abandoned. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.tag steps 'Check Existing Tag', 'Add Current Version Tag'. [git-tag-entrypoint, git-tag-dockerfile, git-tag-readme, checkout-readme]
- **Pass AUTH_KEY and AUTH_SECRET to tests.yml by name instead of `secrets: inherit`. This works even when they exist only as Release environment secrets. Keep `required: true`, and fail the 'Create Test Settings' step when a value is empty.** `inherit` hands every repository and environment-visible secret (including NUGET_USER) to the called workflow. `required: true` checks only that the caller passed the secret, not that it has a value. An unpassed environment secret resolves to an empty string with no error, so the live-API tests fail late and confusingly instead of at setup. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.tests (secrets: inherit); .github/workflows/tests.yml :: on.workflow_call.secrets. [gh-reuse, zizmor-audits]
- **Keep `environment:` on the jobs inside tests.yml, not on the calling job. Consider `environment: { name: Release, deployment: false }` for the test legs, or a separate test environment, so the six matrix jobs stop being Release deployments.** A job that calls a reusable workflow cannot use `environment`, so environment secrets only reach jobs that declare it inside tests.yml. Today every test leg references the same environment that gates publishing, so it shares that environment's protection rules and deployment history. `deployment: false` (since 2026-03-19) still applies required reviewers and wait timers but cannot be combined with custom deployment protection rules. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: jobs.test-linux.environment, jobs.test-netfx.environment. [gh-reuse, gh-deployment-false, gh-environments]
- **Set `if-no-files-found: error` on the upload-artifact step that carries the .nupkg.** The default is `warn`: if pack writes nothing to nuget/, build-package still passes. In the current job order the tag job then pushes `v<Version>` and publish fails at download, leaving a release tag with no package on nuget.org. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.build-package step 'Upload Artifact'. [upload-readme]
- **Make a release run fail loudly when there is nothing to publish, and tag only after a successful publish. Concretely: fail (not skip) when `v<Version>` already exists. Fail when the version is already on nuget.org: drop `--skip-duplicate` so the 409 Conflict fails the push. Fail on an empty artifact (`if-no-files-found: error`). Order the jobs tests -> build-package -> publish -> tag.** `--skip-duplicate` turns nuget.org's 409 Conflict into a warning, and the tag step is skipped when the tag exists. A forgotten `<Version>` bump therefore gives a green NuGet Deploy run that publishes nothing. Tagging before publishing leaves `v<Version>` pointing at a commit with no package whenever publish fails, and the next run then skips the tag. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.tag step 'Check Existing Tag' / 'Add Current Version Tag' (if: exists != 'true'); .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.publish step 'Publish NuGet packages to NuGet' (--skip-duplicate), jobs.publish.needs [tag]; .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.build-package step 'Upload Artifact'. [dotnet-nuget-push, upload-readme, git-tag-entrypoint]
  This repo: Known deviation: tag-if-missing + --skip-duplicate, with tag before publish (.github/workflows/deploy.yml jobs.tag and jobs.publish; documented in CLAUDE.md 'Release' and .claude/skills/bump-version/SKILL.md 'Don't reuse an existing tag'). Fix: make 'Check Existing Tag' exit 1 when the tag exists, remove `--skip-duplicate` from the push, add `if-no-files-found: error` to 'Upload Artifact', and move tagging after publish (`publish.needs: [build-package]`, `tag.needs: [publish]`). Then update CLAUDE.md and the bump-version/release-pack skills to say an unbumped version fails the deploy.
- **Never give the caller (deploy.yml) and the callee (tests.yml) the same concurrency group, and do not set `cancel-in-progress: true` on deploy.** A called workflow evaluates its `concurrency` with the caller's `github` context. With the default `queue: single`, a newer queued run cancels the pending one in its group, so a standalone Tests dispatch on the same ref while a deploy's tests are pending cancels the deploy's tests, and the deploy fails. Reusing one group with cancel-in-progress cancels the run already in progress. `queue: max` (up to 100 pending) is the documented alternative and cannot be combined with cancel-in-progress. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: concurrency (tests-<repo>-<ref>); .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: concurrency (deploy-<repo>-<ref>). [gh-concurrency, gh-reuse-ref]
- **Remember that `dotnet-version` in the matrix installs a runtime/SDK but does not choose the SDK that builds. With no global.json, `dotnet` uses the newest SDK on the runner, preinstalled ones included. Adding a global.json changes the SDK for every leg and every job at once.** The net8.0 leg is built by whatever newest SDK the image has, not SDK 8. A global.json pinned below 10.0 would make the test project (which lists net10.0 in TargetFrameworks) fail to restore on every leg. setup-dotnet v5.4.0+ also rejects wildcard or runtime-style versions in global.json when `rollForward` is set. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: jobs.test-linux.strategy.matrix.dotnet-version; no global.json in the repo; tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj :: TargetFrameworks. [setup-dotnet-readme, setup-dotnet-releases]

## Bug categories

| Category | Look for | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| `expression-injection-in-run` (blocker) | `${{ inputs.* }}`, `${{ secrets.* }}`, `${{ github.event.* }}`, `${{ github.head_ref }}` or step outputs written directly into a `run:` body (bash or pwsh), especially inside quoted strings. | A crafted input or a secret with shell metacharacters runs commands on the runner or silently corrupts the value, in a job that holds live API credentials or release scopes. [gh-script-injection, gh-use-secrets] |
| `excess-token-scope` (confirm) | Write scopes or `id-token: write` at workflow level, or on jobs that do not push tags or publish. New jobs without a `permissions:` block in a workflow that relies on job-level raises. | A compromised or buggy step can push refs, act on runs, or mint an OIDC token that nuget.org exchanges for a push key. [gh-secure-use, gh-workflow-syntax, nuget-tp] |
| `mutable-action-ref` (confirm) | Any `uses: owner/repo@<tag or branch>` (first-party included) not covered by actions.lock, Docker actions built from unpinned base images, and SHA pins whose version comment is missing or stale. | The code that runs in the release job changes without a commit to this repo (supply-chain takeover of the publish key or tag push). [gh-secure-use, gh-lockfiles, git-tag-dockerfile] |
| `silent-release-step` (blocker) | Release steps that succeed without doing their job: curl without `-f` or response checks, `--skip-duplicate`, `if-no-files-found: warn`, `if:` conditions that skip the tag or push, `continue-on-error`, and a tag pushed before the publish succeeds. | A green NuGet Deploy run with no package published, a tag without a package, or a moved release tag. [git-tag-entrypoint, dotnet-nuget-push, upload-readme] |
| `trusted-publishing-claim-drift` (blocker) | A renamed deploy.yml, a changed or removed `environment: Release` on the publish job, publish moved into another file or a reusable workflow, NuGet/login moved away from the push step, or `id-token: write` removed. | NuGet/login fails (no matching policy, or 403 without id-token), or the key expires before the push, so the release is blocked. [nuget-tp, nuget-login] |
| `secret-scope-leak` (confirm) | `secrets: inherit` on reusable calls, test or PR jobs that reference the Release environment, files written with secrets (tests/Transloadit.Tests/appsettings.Tests.json) inside a path later uploaded as an artifact, and secrets echoed or used in `if:`. | Credentials reach jobs or artifacts that do not need them, or appear in logs. Rotation is then required. [gh-reuse, gh-use-secrets, gh-secure-use, zizmor-audits] |
| `reusable-contract-drift` (confirm) | An input or secret added to only one of `on.workflow_call` / `on.workflow_dispatch` in tests.yml, or a caller (`deploy.yml` jobs.tests `with:`/`secrets:`) that does not match the callee's declarations. | `inputs.x` or `secrets.X` is empty on one trigger path. Tests then run against an empty NotifyUrl or empty credentials, or the call fails validation at dispatch time. [gh-reuse, gh-workflow-syntax] |
| `concurrency-pending-cancel` (suggestion) | Shared or overlapping `concurrency.group` values between deploy.yml and tests.yml or other workflows, `cancel-in-progress: true` on release paths, and reliance on the default `queue: single`. | A queued deploy, or the deploy's test stage, is cancelled by a later dispatch, and the release silently does not happen. [gh-concurrency, gh-reuse-ref] |

## Wiring

- Every job that tags or publishes transitively `needs` the whole test matrix. Today the chain is tests -> build-package -> tag -> publish; the target order is tests -> build-package -> publish -> tag (tag only after a successful publish). Fails as: Removing a `needs` edge can publish an untested package. Tagging before publish leaves a tag with no package when publish fails.. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.*.needs. [gh-workflow-syntax, dotnet-nuget-push]
- The artifact name `nuget` and path match between upload-artifact (build-package) and download-artifact (publish), and both actions are upgraded as a pair. Fails as: Publish fails at download (in the current order, after the tag has already been pushed).. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.build-package step 'Upload Artifact', jobs.publish step 'Download NuGet Artifacts'. [upload-readme, download-readme]
- tests.yml declares `notifyUrl` under both `workflow_call.inputs` and `workflow_dispatch.inputs`, and AUTH_KEY/AUTH_SECRET under `workflow_call.secrets`. deploy.yml jobs.tests passes `with: notifyUrl` and the secrets. Fails as: An empty input or secret on one trigger path, or a validation error at dispatch.. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: on; .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.tests. [gh-reuse]
- The publish job keeps `environment: Release`, `id-token: write`, NuGet/login with `user:` (nuget.org profile name, from secrets.NUGET_USER) and the push in the same job, in the file named deploy.yml. Fails as: No matching Trusted Publishing policy, so the release is blocked.. Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.publish. [nuget-tp, nuget-login]
- Every JavaScript action in use declares a Node runtime the runners still provide (node24). Node 20 was removed from GitHub-hosted runners on 2026-09-23 and the opt-out variable is gone. Fails as: Any action version still declaring node20 fails to start.. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml; .github/workflows/deploy.yml. [gh-node20-removed, nuget-login-action, upload-releases, download-releases, setup-dotnet-releases]

## Testing

Workflow files have no unit tests here. Static checks (actionlint for syntax, expressions, reusable-workflow inputs/secrets and shellcheck of run scripts; zizmor for security audits such as template-injection, excessive-permissions, secrets-inherit, artipacked and unpinned-uses) prove the YAML. Only a real dispatch proves the wiring. Dispatch 'Tests' on the branch to exercise tests.yml. A change to deploy.yml can only be exercised end to end by a real release.

- Harness: not used here yet: no workflow linter is configured (recommended actionlint, optionally zizmor; flag for /stackfoundry:scaffold-test-harness)
- Run: `actionlint`; `gh workflow run Tests -f notifyUrl=<https url> --ref <branch>`
- Trap: Both workflows are workflow_dispatch/workflow_call only, so nothing runs on push or PR. A broken workflow is found only when someone dispatches it.
- Trap: Never dispatch NuGet Deploy to test a workflow change. It pushes a tag and publishes to nuget.org.
- Trap: The test legs hit the live Transloadit API with Release environment secrets, and max-parallel: 1 is deliberate (shared account rate limits, matching the disabled xUnit parallelization).
- Trap: cardinalby/git-tag-action is a Docker action, so it only runs on Linux runners.
- Trap: Release dates on the actions' GitHub release pages carry no year. Check the tag date before assuming how recent a release is.
- Sources: [actionlint, zizmor-audits, gh-reuse, git-tag-readme]

## Performance

- Do not turn on setup-dotnet `cache: true` without committing packages.lock.json files. Caching is off by default, and with caching on the action throws when no lock file exists (the repo has none). Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: step 'Setup .NET'; .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: step 'Setup .NET'. [setup-dotnet-readme]
- `max-parallel: 1` on both matrices serializes the six live-API legs on purpose (shared rate limits). Do not raise it to speed up CI without checking the account limits. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: jobs.test-linux.strategy, jobs.test-netfx.strategy. [gh-workflow-syntax]

## Security

- Set `persist-credentials: false` on checkouts in jobs that never push (both test jobs, build-package). Since checkout v6 the token is stored in a separate file under $RUNNER_TEMP rather than .git/config, but it remains on disk for every later step of the job. Leave the default only where a later step runs authenticated git (the tag job, if it switches to `git push`). Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: step uses actions/checkout; .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.build-package step uses actions/checkout. [checkout-readme, zizmor-audits]
- Test credentials are written to tests/Transloadit.Tests/appsettings.Tests.json in the workspace. Never upload the workspace or the test output directory as an artifact from these jobs, and do not store the credentials as one JSON secret: GitHub redacts individual secret values, and a structured blob is not reliably masked. Here: .github/workflows/tests.yml :: step 'Create Test Settings'. [gh-secure-use]
- If PR-triggered CI is added, do not give PR jobs the Release environment or secrets, and do not use pull_request_target to work around missing secrets. Secrets are not passed to runs triggered from forks, and checkout v7 refuses fork PR code under pull_request_target/workflow_run unless `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout` is set. Here: not used here yet. [gh-use-secrets, checkout-readme]
- The NuGet push key is short-lived (1 hour) and single-use per token, but it is still a credential: pass it to `dotnet nuget push` through `env:` like any other secret, not by interpolating `steps.login.outputs.NUGET_API_KEY` into the script (see the expression-injection rule). Here: .github/workflows/deploy.yml :: jobs.publish step 'Publish NuGet packages to NuGet'. [nuget-tp, gh-use-secrets]

## Upgrades

- Pinned in: .github/workflows/tests.yml: actions/checkout@v6.0.2 (x2), actions/setup-dotnet@v5.2.0 (x2); .github/workflows/deploy.yml: actions/checkout@v6.0.2 (x2), actions/setup-dotnet@v5.2.0 (x3), actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.1, actions/download-artifact@v8.0.1, cardinalby/git-tag-action@v1.0, NuGet/login@v1
- Moves with: actions/upload-artifact v7.x with actions/download-artifact v8.x: the same @actions/artifact backend generation (v7.0.2 and v8.0.2 both move to @actions/artifact 6.3.1). Upgrade together and re-run a full deploy path.; Bump the same action identically in tests.yml and deploy.yml. Both files pin each action version separately.; NuGet/login and the nuget.org Trusted Publishing policy: a policy change (workflow file, environment) must land before the matching workflow change.
- Release notes: https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases · https://github.com/actions/setup-dotnet/releases · https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases · https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases · https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-23-node-20-is-no-longer-available-in-github-actions/
- Migration guides: https://github.com/actions/checkout · https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles
